extracted.intended_audience: Postdoctoral researchers applying for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (Horizon Europe)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting an MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal (2026 call), including eligibility, finding a host, drafting the proposal, and submission procedures. Targets researchers and prospective host organisations/supervisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD requirement (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD degree on the closing date for applications. Applicants who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree are also eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify your status against the call deadline; consult the Guide for Applicants and National Contact Points if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum 8 years research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a maximum of eight years of experience in research from the date of the award of the PhD degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain types of time are excluded from this calculation (years of experience outside research and career breaks; years of experience in research in third countries for nationals/long-term residents of EU Member States or Associated Countries reintegrating to Europe). Use the REA self-assessment tool and the specific guidelines on calculation of 8-years research experience to check your eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with mobility rules: they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the beneficiary (for European Postdoctoral Fellowships), or the host organisation for the outgoing phase (for Global Postdoctoral Fellowships) for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the call deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the list of participating/associated countries for Horizon Europe and consult the Work Programme for specific exceptions and conditions; National Contact Points can advise on borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation and joint submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are made jointly by the researcher and a prospective beneficiary (main host organisation) located in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Organisations from all socioeconomic sectors and many institution types can host fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable hosts include higher education institutions, research centres and infrastructures, private-sector organisations (industry, SMEs), public-sector organisations (governments, agencies, museums), certain international organisations, NGOs, foundations, charities, etc. For Global Fellowships and short secondments, organisations in third countries not associated to Horizon Europe may host under specific conditions (see Work Programme). Use MSCA Matchmaking, Euraxess hosting offers, and Partner Search announcements to find hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor and host commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your prospective supervisor can dedicate sufficient time to support your application and, if successful, the project; supervisors and host institutions may be involved in multiple proposals but an individual researcher can submit only one proposal per call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss and confirm supervisor availability and level of commitment early. Note the guidance that supervisors involved in a large number of proposals per call do not necessarily achieve high success rates — quality of engagement matters more than quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: One proposal per researcher rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual researcher can only submit one proposal per call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors and host institutions may participate in multiple proposals, but applicants must choose a single submission. Plan collaborations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official guidance and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should consult the Guide for Applicants, MSCA Work Programme (including Award Criteria and budget structure), proposal templates, evaluation guidelines, and other REA-published resources to prepare their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific resources include: Guide for Applicants, a guide to avoid common mistakes in Postdoctoral Fellowships proposals, proposal templates, evaluation forms, and other handbooks. The RADIANCE project and National Contact Points provide complementary/unofficial support. Follow templates closely to avoid formal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award criteria and budget structure (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSCA Work Programme contains the Award Criteria and budget structure (referenced pages: p.77 and 83) which govern how proposals are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Work Programme pages for the precise award criteria and how budget items are structured. Use the evaluation forms (available) to understand expert reviewers' scoring and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender dimension and inclusiveness (evaluation aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender dimension and inclusiveness are aspects evaluated under the award criteria (see Horizon Europe Programme Guide p.16-20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address gender considerations in research design, recruitment, and project activities where relevant. Consult the Programme Guide for specific expectations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and exploitation of research (evaluation aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissemination and exploitation of research are evaluated aspects (see Horizon Europe Programme Guide p.31-39).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan clear dissemination routes, open access outputs, stakeholder engagement, and exploitation paths (impact and use). Describe expected outputs, target audiences, and measures to ensure uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science (evaluation aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open science is an evaluated aspect of proposals (see Horizon Europe Programme Guide p.40-55).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how you will implement open access to publications and data, FAIR data practices, preregistration or open methodologies where appropriate, and how openness supports quality and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and MSCA Green Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are strongly encouraged to adopt sustainable practices in line with the EU green objectives and the MSCA Green Charter and to report on their efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sustainable practices in project planning (e.g., reduced travel, green procurement, energy-efficient lab practices) and report them. The page points to useful tips and guidance to increase project sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek external review and support before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your draft application with your supervisor, host organisation, MSCA National Contact Points, Marie Curie Alumni Association, and former awardees to receive feedback and improve your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use webinars, matchmaking events, bootcamps, hands-on workshops, and host-provided training. Some National Contact Points offer pre-submission checks in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the proposal through the Funding & Tenders Opportunities Portal before the deadline; proposals can be updated, downloaded, or withdrawn until the deadline. To avoid last-minute problems, submit early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2026 Postdoctoral Fellowships call opens 9 April 2026 and closes 9 September 2026, 17:00 CEST. Familiarise yourself with the portal’s online manual and submission workflows. The evaluation process takes approximately five months (results expected around February 2027).

rubrics_metrics.name: ERA Fellowships opt-in for widening hosts
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying for a standard European Fellowship with a host from a Widening Country and outermost regions, you may opt in to the 2026 ERA Fellowships call when submitting your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Around 40 ERA Fellowships may be awarded to excellent applicants not selected under MSCA due to budget constraints; consult the ERA Fellowships eligibility and list of eligible host countries.
